chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ahmad ibn Umar, who said:

I asked Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام about a man who forgot the two rak'ahs of the obligatory tawaf and had already circumambulated the House until he came to Minā. He said: 'He should return to the Maqam of Ibrahim عليه السلام and perform them.'

key_terms.الْبَيْتِ: the Sacred House, meaning the Ka'bah
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْ: the two units of prayer required after tawaf
key_terms.طَوَافِ الْفَرِيضَةِ: the obligatory circumambulation of the Ka'bah
key_terms.فَلْيُصَلِّهِمَا: let him perform the two missed rak'ahs
key_terms.مَقَامِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the Station of Ibrahim عليه السلام, where the prayer of tawaf is performed
key_terms.مِنًى: Minā, the pilgrimage site to which the person had proceeded

ai.seo_question: What should someone do if he forgets the two rak'ahs of the obligatory tawaf and has already gone to Minā?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgets the two rak'ahs of the obligatory tawaf. Even after proceeding to Minā, he must return to the Maqam of Ibrahim عليه السلام and perform the missed prayer there.
